question: What is the difference between the average of prime numbers between 20 and 40 and the average of multiples of 2 between 10 and 30?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Primes between 20 and 40 ⇒ 23, 29, 31, 37

Average = (23 + 29 + 31 + 37)/4 = 120/4 = 30

Multiples of 2 between 10 and 30 ⇒ 12, 14, ..., 28

AP ⇒ average = (first + last)/2 = (12 + 28)/2 = 20

Difference = 30 − 20 = 10

**∴ Answer = 10**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Prime numbers between 20 and 40

Multiples of 2 between 10 and 30

**Formula used:**

Average = Sum ÷ Number of terms

For AP: Average = (first + last)/2

**Calculation:**

⇒ Primes: 23, 29, 31, 37

⇒ Average = (23 + 29 + 31 + 37)/4 = 120/4 = 30

⇒ Multiples of 2: 12 to 28

⇒ Average = (12 + 28)/2 = 20

⇒ Difference = 30 − 20 = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Prime Numbers

Numbers divisible only by 1 and itself

Arithmetic Progression

Even numbers form an AP

Average Trick

For equally spaced numbers, average = midpoint

Key Insight

Use midpoint formula to save time
